sections.content: How many people stayed in Leighton Buzzard after gaining qualifications?

Leighton Buzzard is a medium-sized town in the East of England. Leighton Buzzard does not have its own university.

Leighton Buzzard has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Leighton Buzzard ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,795 state-school pupils from Leighton Buzzard who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 595 (33%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 505 (28%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Leighton Buzzard to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Leighton Buzzard's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Leighton Buzzard in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Leighton Buzzard move to?

Of Leighton Buzzard's graduates, 245 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 30 of those graduates (12%) were living fairly locally, in the Milton Keynes travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Leighton Buzzard's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 140 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 50 of those qualified non-graduates (36%) were living fairly locally, in the Milton Keynes travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Leighton Buzzard's GCSE cohort:

  • 215 graduates left the East of England
  • the most common region they moved to was the South East
  • 105 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the East of England
  • the most common region they moved to was the South East

In 2018 to 2019, 36% of graduates and 33% of qualified non-graduates living in Leighton Buzzard had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 530 graduates and 540 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Leighton Buzzard. This is compared with the 595 graduates and 505 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 64% of the graduates had also lived in Leighton Buzzard as GCSE pupils, while 36% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Leighton Buzzard in 2018 to 2019, 66% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 33% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
